artifacts.synopsis: Seven members of a PCA mission church were tried and censured by a provisional Session for opposing the organizing minister's continuation as permanent pastor. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the convictions, holding that the indictments lacked required specificity under BCO 32-5, that the accused had no sinned against the fifth or ninth commandment by expressing opinions about ministerial suitability, and that the right to choose a pastor belongs to the congregation—not the provisional Session. A concurring opinion addressed indictment requirements, standard of review in appeals, and congregational rights in mission church minister selection.

artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint of TE Art Sartorius and six others against Presbytery of Siouxlands, finding that the Presbytery erred when it approved its Judicial Commission's verdict acquitting TE Gregory Lawrence of five charges related to Federal Vision theology and unconventional views on baptism and apostasy. The SJC identified serious procedural errors, specifically that the Judicial Commission admitted exculpatory post-indictment written statements from the defendant without subjecting them to cross-examination, contrary to BCO 35-5. The case was remanded to Presbytery for a new trial with detailed instructions regarding evidence procedures and Presbytery oversight.

artifacts.title: Ehrlich v. North Georgia
artifacts.synopsis: Complaint of Devin and Tracey Ehrlich against North Georgia Presbytery regarding the Presbytery's denial of the Ehrlichs' complaint about the Intown Community Church Session's instruction prohibiting distribution of an open letter criticizing a pastor under investigation. The SJC held that the Session acted within its authority in preventing distribution of the letter, as it would disturb the peace of the church after the Presbytery had investigated and dismissed the underlying allegations against the pastor.

artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission declined to adjudicate a reference from Central Carolina Presbytery regarding complaints by William A. Conrad against the Interim Session of Prosperity Presbyterian Church. The panel found that additional related complaints had been lodged that were not formally referred to the Commission, and adjudicating the referred matters would render these additional complaints moot without giving them proper consideration under BCO 41-5. The case was referred back to the Central Carolina Presbytery.

artifacts.title: Morse v. Covenant Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission addressed three issues regarding actions of Covenant Presbytery involving TE Daniel R. Morse and Grace Presbyterian Church. The Commission ruled that teaching elders Morse and Crenshaw, having renounced communion with the PCA by joining the Reformed Episcopal Church, should be removed from presbytery rolls under BCO 38-3. The Commission found no provision requiring churches to notify presbytery before withdrawing from the PCA. Finally, the Commission determined that receiving and recording a protest is an administrative act, not a judicial decision, and that complaints regarding such actions are barred by BCO 45-5.
